sections.h2: What a quitclaim deed does in Kansas
sections.html:
With a quitclaim, the signer passes along whatever share of the land they hold, and promises nothing about its quality. K.S.A. 58-2204 gives the short form: "A.B. quitclaims to C.D.," followed by the description of the premises and the consideration, signed and acknowledged by the grantor.

Compare it with a warranty deed. A warranty deed is the seller's guarantee that title is clean and that earlier owners or heirs hold no claim. A quitclaim simply releases the name of someone who may have an interest. That is why quitclaims show up between family members, after a divorce or when co-owners shuffle names, and why a buyer in an ordinary sale usually asks for a warranty deed.

sections.h2: What the register of deeds needs before recording
sections.html:
A deed has to name both parties, describe the land, carry a proper notary acknowledgment and come with a sales validation questionnaire or a stated exemption. Johnson County and Wyandotte County apply nearly identical rules, which follow the statutes (K.S.A. 58-2205, 58-2209, 58-2211, 58-2221).

  • The grantor's name, the grantee's name and the legal description of the property.
  • Signatures that are properly notarized, with the full date, the notary's appointment expiration date and the state and county where the act took place.
  • A notary certificate with no blanks, the notary's seal and a signer name that matches the name in the deed.
  • Page one with a 3-inch top margin and 1-inch margins on the other three sides, with 1-inch margins on every later page, on letter-size paper.
  • The full name and mailing address of the person receiving the property, which the register forwards to the county clerk for tax statements.

Johnson County cannot accept a document for recording by email or fax. Bring it in person, mail it with a return envelope or use an approved electronic recording vendor. If a document misses the margin rules, K.S.A. 28-115 lets the register add a sheet for the recording information or copy the document, and those extra pages are charged. Illegible documents can be rejected.

Usually a questionnaire is required, unless one of the statutory exemptions applies and the deed says so. K.S.A. 79-1437c bars recording of a deed that arrives without the questionnaire, and K.S.A. 79-1437e lists the exempt transfers. An exemption must be clearly stated on the document being filed. The register cannot add it for you.

Transfers exempt from the questionnaire under K.S.A. 79-1437e
Exempt transferTypical quitclaim use
Gift, donation or contribution stated in the deedFamily transfer with no payment
Divorce settlementOne spouse deeds out to the other
Solely to create a joint tenancy or tenancy in commonOwner adds a co-owner
To or from a trust without considerationMoving a house into or out of a trust
Quitclaim filed to clear title encumbrancesClearing a cloud on title
Correcting a recorded deed with no added considerationFixing a name or description
Transfer by a fiduciary under judicial orderExecutor or conservator conveyance

What a buyer paid stays out of the public record (K.S.A. 79-1437f). The questionnaires are kept for five years and are not filed of record.

State law (K.S.A. 28-115) sets recording fees, and each register's office posts the totals. In Wyandotte County a deed costs $21 for page one and $17 for every page after it. Plain copies are $1 per page, with $13 more for a certified copy.

Each county posts its own schedule. Phone the register where the property is located before mailing a check. Wyandotte requires payment in advance for copy requests, and its recording desk takes checks payable to the Register of Deeds. Johnson County accepts walk-ins on weekdays, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

These fees cover recording only. A lawyer's time or a title company's charges are separate, so budget for them if you want help preparing the deed.

sections.h2: When a quitclaim makes sense, and when it does not
sections.html:
A quitclaim works best when everyone already agrees who should hold title and nobody needs a guarantee. It is a poor fit when someone is paying for the property and expects clean title.

  • Good fit: putting a spouse or relative on or off the title, moving a house into a trust, releasing a possible claim of a former co-owner.
  • Works poorly: a sale to a buyer who will ask for a warranty deed, or a transfer meant to settle a dispute about ownership that has not actually been resolved.
  • Cannot do: change a recorded document. A recorded deed is a permanent record, so any change to the title requires a new document to be prepared and recorded.

Register staff cannot draft your deed or advise you on the wording. Use a lawyer or a title company, though a person is allowed to make out their own deed. Wyandotte posts blank sample forms for a general quitclaim deed and a joint tenancy quitclaim deed on its website.

sections.h2: Selling a house after a quitclaim deed
sections.html:
Once the recorded deed shows the right owners, those owners can sign the sale deed. A quitclaim often comes first in family situations. Heirs deed the house among themselves, or a parent deeds it to a child, and then the new owner decides to sell.

Check three things before listing or taking an offer. First, confirm the quitclaim was recorded in the county where the house sits, because K.S.A. 58-2221 sends recording to that county's register of deeds. Second, confirm the mortgage and tax balances, since a deed changes ownership on the record and does not remove either. Third, if the house came to you through a death, read our pages on the Kansas probate process and the transfer on death deed, because a court order or an earlier TOD deed may control who can sign.

We buy Kansas houses as-is, including homes where the title paperwork is still being sorted out. A title company will review the recorded deeds before closing, so having your quitclaim and its recording stamp ready speeds up that review.

Check recorded documents and keep a copy of anything you sign. Fake or forced deeds are a recognized problem, and Wyandotte County posts a property fraud alert in English and Spanish that links to PropertyFraudAlert.com. A quitclaim moves ownership without a warranty, so be wary of anyone who asks you to sign one quickly, and have a lawyer look at it first.

sections.h2: Steps to record your own quitclaim
sections.html: Start with the current deed so you can copy the legal description exactly. Prepare the new deed with both names and the grantee's mailing address, then sign it in front of a notary. Complete the sales validation questionnaire or write the exemption into the deed. Finally, take the packet to the register of deeds in the county where the land sits and pay the recording fee.

faqs.q: What is the Kansas statute for a quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: K.S.A. 58-2204 sets out the short form, "A.B. quitclaims to C.D.," with a description of the premises and the consideration, signed and acknowledged by the grantor. Recording is handled under K.S.A. 58-2221.

faqs.q: Where do I record a quitclaim deed in Kansas?
faqs.a: With the register of deeds in the county where the land is located. In Johnson County that means the office in Olathe, and in Wyandotte County it is at the courthouse in Kansas City, Kansas.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed need to be notarized in Kansas?
faqs.a: Yes. The signature must be acknowledged before a notary, with the full date, the notary's expiration date, the jurisdiction and the notary's seal on the certificate. An incomplete certificate gets the document returned.

faqs.q: Do I need a sales validation questionnaire for a quitclaim?
faqs.a: Usually, unless an exemption in K.S.A. 79-1437e applies, such as a gift stated in the deed or a divorce settlement. If an exemption applies, the deed itself must say so.

faqs.q: Can the register of deeds help me write a quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: No. The register of deeds is a records custodian and can answer general process questions only. Use a lawyer or a title company for drafting.
